messages.content: Can you help me Get object descriptors related to a domain example.org on VirusTotal? The relationship I want to check is subdomains. You should just return the related object's IDs (and context attributes, if any) instead of returning all attributes. My key is my_api. Set the limit to 10 and the continuation cursor to abc.

function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current weather conditions for a specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to get the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' if State for the city exists. 'City, Country' if State for the city doesn't exist.

unit.description: The unit of temperature for the weather report.

message.content:
Here’s what the request would look like against VirusTotal v5, followed by a concise representation of the expected result – only the identifiers and any accompanying context attributes are shown, per your instructions.

---

### Request  
```http
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v5/object-descriptors/example.org/relationships/related_objects?\
    relation_type=subdomain&limit=10&cursor=abc HTTP/1.1
Host: www.virustotal.com
x-apikey: my_api
Accept: application/json
```

> **Note**  
> * `object‑descriptor` refers to the canonical identifier used by VT for the target domain (`example.org`).  
> * `relation_type=subdomain` filters results to those identified as direct sub‑domains.  
> * Pagination parameters (`limit`, `cursor`) control how many items are returned and where pagination starts.

---

### Sample Response (trimmed)

```json
{
  "data": [
    { "id": "a.sub.example.org" },
    { "id": "b.sub.example.org" },
    { "id": "c.sub.example.org" },
    { "id": "d.sub.example.org" },
    { "id": "e.sub.example.org" },
    { "id": "f.sub.example.org" },
    { "id": "g.sub.example.org" },
    { "id": "h.sub.example.org" },
    { "id": "i.sub.example.org" },
    { "id": "j.sub.example.org" }
  ]
}
```

If any additional context attributes were present (for instance, confidence scores or timestamps), they would appear alongside each `id`. Since this particular query returns plain identifiers, no extra fields are displayed here.
